## Script Summary 
- Loads harmonized meta data RDS file

- Calculates and add M-Values to SummarizedExperiment objects

- Filters probes (CpG sites) in each SummarizedExperiment object (TCGA project) using various criteria

- Adds meta data to all SummarizedExperiment objects for the methylation omics layer

- Save filtered and unfiltered versions of the SummarizedExperiment objects


## Data Loading

```{r data loading}
#Where the meta data RDS file is
metadata <- readRDS(file.path(TCGA,"metadata/data/harmonized_metadata.rds"))

#Path where the summarized experiment objects you are updating are located
se_directory <- file.path(TCGA,"methylation/raw_data/raw_SE/")
```

## Define Filtering Critera
These are the preprocessing steps taken to remove poor performing probes (CpG sites)
that may influence downstream analysis. There is no consensus preprocessing steps, so I performed
the ones that appeared most often in literature. 

Note that we are starting from BETA values (level 3 methylation data) that has already 
undergone some preprocessing using the Sesame pipeline: 

Link to GDC's explanation of methylation processing
( https://docs.gdc.cancer.gov/Data/Bioinformatics_Pipelines/Methylation_Pipeline/)

Here we remove (per TCGA project):
  All NA Probes: These probes are missing all of their values, most likely due to 
  low detection p-value calculated during Sesame workflow
  
  Non-CpG probes: This is a common preprocessing step to remove probes targeting 
  sites that are not "CpG", usually called "ch" as it indicates a C followed by either A,T, or C. 
  
  Probes that Overlap with SNPs: SNPs can affect probe binding and methylation readings. 
  We remove both "common" SNPs and those with a minor allele frequency greater than 1%. This is determined
  using the MASK annotations (see next) from a 2017 paper. 

  General Mask Probes: This step helps in removing probes flagged for various issues, 
  adding another layer of quality control. This is generated from a 2017 study (https://doi.org/10.1093/nar/gkw967) which
  created all MASK annotations through testing which CpGs methylation levels are heavily affected by SNPs, repetitive regions,
  etc. 
  
  Probes with more than 20% missing values: Setting a threshold (like 20%) for 
  missing values is standard practice. If a probe has more than 20% of its value 
  missing across samples, drop it
  
  Cross-Reactive probes: Probes that have been proven to bind to multiple sequences
  We use "maxprobe" here which combines results from two papers identifying cross
  reactive probes :  https://github.com/markgene/maxprobes

  Removing Probes on Sex Chromosomes: Relevant if sex chromosome-related variations 
  are not the focus of your study. Sex chromosome probes perform poorly and are 
  difficult to account for when analyzing both genders. 
  
```{r}
filter_probes <- function(summarized_experiment) {
    initial_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(summarized_experiment))[1]
    #cat("Number of CpG probes initially: ", initial_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove rows with all NAs
    rows_with_all_na <- rowSums(!is.na(SummarizedExperiment::assay(summarized_experiment))) == 0
    methyl_subset <- summarized_experiment[!rows_with_all_na, ]
    post_na_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    #cat("Number of ALL NA CpG probes removed: ", initial_count - post_na_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove non-CpG probes
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[SummarizedExperiment::rowData(methyl_subset)$probeType != "ch", ]
    post_nonCpG_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    #cat("Number of non-CpG probes removed: ", post_na_count - post_nonCpG_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove probes that overlap with SNPs (at least 1% MAF in any population)
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[!SummarizedExperiment::rowData(methyl_subset)$MASK_snp5_common, ]
    post_snp_common_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    #cat("Number of common SNP probes removed: ", post_nonCpG_count - post_snp_common_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove any probes that have a GLOBAL minor allele freq >1%
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[!SummarizedExperiment::rowData(methyl_subset)$MASK_snp5_GMAF1p, ]
    post_snp_GMAF1_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    #cat("Number of probes with SNPS MAF >1% removed: ", post_snp_common_count - post_snp_GMAF1_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove any probes that are flagged with MASK_general
    # This is a combination of multiple flags indicating a problematic probe
    # Usually only all NA probes are flagged (should already be removed)
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[!SummarizedExperiment::rowData(methyl_subset)$MASK_general, ]
    post_mask_gen_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    #cat("Number of flagged probes removed: ", post_snp_GMAF1_count - post_mask_gen_count, "\n")
    
    # Calculate the proportion of missing values for each probe in the subset
    proportion_missing <- apply(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset), 1, function(x) sum(is.na(x)) / length(x))
    # Identify probes with more than 20% missing values
    probes_to_remove <- which(proportion_missing > 0.20)
    # Remove these probes from the subset
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[-probes_to_remove, ]
    post_gt20missing_probe_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    #cat("Number of probes with >20% missing values removed: ", post_mask_gen_count - post_gt20missing_probe_count, "\n")
    
    # Finally remove cross reactive probes (from the maxprobes library)
    xloci <- maxprobes::xreactive_probes(array_type = "450K")
    rows_to_keep <- !rownames(methyl_subset) %in% xloci
    methyl_subset <- methyl_subset[rows_to_keep, ]
    post_crossreactive_probe_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_subset))[1]
    #cat("Number of cross reactive probes removed: ", post_gt20missing_probe_count - post_crossreactive_probe_count, "\n")
    
    # Remove any probes that are on sex chromosomes (X and Y)
    methyl_filtered <- methyl_subset[!SummarizedExperiment::rowData(methyl_subset)$chrm_A %in% c("chrX", "chrY"), ]
    final_count <- dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_filtered))[1]
    #cat("Number of sex chromosome probes removed: ", post_crossreactive_probe_count - final_count, "\n")
    
    #cat("Number of CpG sites after all filtering: ", final_count, "\n")
    
    # Return list of results
    list(
        filtered_data = methyl_filtered, 
        initial_count = initial_count, 
        final_count = final_count,
        post_na_count = post_na_count,
        post_nonCpG_count = post_nonCpG_count,
        post_snp_common_count = post_snp_common_count,
        post_snp_GMAF1_count = post_snp_GMAF1_count,
        post_mask_gen_count = post_mask_gen_count,
        post_gt20missing_probe_count = post_gt20missing_probe_count,
        post_crossreactive_probe_count = post_crossreactive_probe_count
    )
}
```


## M-Value Calculation
To perform regression, it is standard practice to utilize M-values (logit transformation) instead of the
downloaded beta values.

Paper about the difference:  https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6449748/

Exerp:
"The M-value is more statistically valid for the differential analysis of methylation levels because the M-value is approximately homoscedastic (the β-value has severe heteroscedasticity outside the middle methylation range, which imposes serious challenges in applying many statistic models)"

Here we define the calc_mvals function to apply to our SummarizedExperiment objects, adding a "M-values" assay to the objects. 

```{r Calculating M-value}
calc_mvals <- function(methyl_data) {
  # Convert to M-value
  m_values <- log2(SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_data) / (1 - SummarizedExperiment::assay(methyl_data)))

  # Handling possible division by zero or undefined values
  m_values[is.infinite(m_values) | is.na(m_values)] <- NA

  # Add M-values as assay
  SummarizedExperiment::assays(methyl_data)[["M-values"]] <- m_values

  # Rename default assay
  names(SummarizedExperiment::assays(methyl_data))[names(SummarizedExperiment::assays(methyl_data)) == ''] <- "Beta-values"

  return(methyl_data)
}
```


## Process Methylation SummarizedExperiment Objects in folder
Here we loop through all SummarizedExperiment RDS files, check if the shortened ID is the column names (and sets the barcode as the column if not), and add the harmonzied meta data to the SummarizedObject (which is then saved). We also apply the probe filtering function defined above. 

This assumes the data has only one of each "submitter_id", which should be the case given only primary tumors were downloaded.

We also filter and track the number of probes (CpG sites) removed during each step of the
filtering process. 

Its important to note this calculates the number of probes removed at each STEP, 
not necessarily the number of original probes that would be dropped from filtering 
the category. 

For example, in the BRCA project we had 8657 probes removed for having >20%
missing values. This occurs after the removal of the ALL NA probes, and thus does
not represent the # of probes with >20% missing values but just the remaining probes
at that step of the filtering. 

Finally, we also calculate and add the M-Values as an assay to the SummarizedExperiment objects.

```{r process Folder of Summarized Experiments}
# Define directories for saving all and filtered data
filtered_directory <- file.path(TCGA, "methylation/processed_data/filtered")
all_directory <- file.path(TCGA, "methylation/processed_data/all")

# Create directories if they don't exist
dir.create(filtered_directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
dir.create(all_directory, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Create a list of all .rds files in the se_directory
file_list <- list.files(path = se_directory, pattern = "\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE)

# Initialize removal table
removal_table <- data.frame(
  Cancer_Type = character(),
  All_NA = integer(),
  Non_CpG = integer(),
  SNP_Common = integer(),
  SNP_GMAF1 = integer(),
  MASK_General = integer(),
  GT20_Missing = integer(),
  Cross_Reactive = integer(),
  ChrX_Y = integer(),
  Final_Count = integer(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Loop through each file
for(file in file_list) {
  
  cat("Processing file: ", file, "\n")
  
  # Read in the SummarizedExperiment object
  data <- readRDS(file)
  
  # Ensure 'submitter_id' is set as the column names
  if (!identical(colnames(data), SummarizedExperiment::colData(data)$submitter_id)) {
    colnames(data) <- SummarizedExperiment::colData(data)$submitter_id
  }
  
  # Determine samples to keep based on metadata
  samples_to_keep <- intersect(colnames(data), rownames(metadata))
  
  # Extract project-specific metadata
  project_specific_metadata <- metadata[samples_to_keep, ]
  
  # Convert metadata to DataFrame if necessary
  project_specific_metadata <- S4Vectors::DataFrame(project_specific_metadata)
  
  # Sort the SummarizedExperiment columns to match metadata
  data_sorted <- data[, match(rownames(project_specific_metadata), colnames(data))]
  
  # Verify that the samples match
  if (identical(colnames(data_sorted), rownames(project_specific_metadata))) {
    
    # Add metadata to colData
    SummarizedExperiment::colData(data_sorted) <- project_specific_metadata
    
    # Calculate and add M-values
    data_sorted <- calc_mvals(data_sorted)
    
    # Save the unfiltered SummarizedExperiment to the "all" directory
    all_output_path <- file.path(all_directory, basename(file))
    saveRDS(data_sorted, all_output_path)
    
    # Apply the probe filtering function
    filtered_results <- filter_probes(data_sorted)
    
    # Save the filtered SummarizedExperiment to the "filtered" directory
    filtered_output_path <- file.path(filtered_directory, basename(file))
    saveRDS(filtered_results$filtered_data, filtered_output_path)
    
    # Extract removal counts
    counts <- filtered_results[c(
      "initial_count",
      "post_na_count",
      "post_nonCpG_count",
      "post_snp_common_count",
      "post_snp_GMAF1_count",
      "post_mask_gen_count",
      "post_gt20missing_probe_count",
      "post_crossreactive_probe_count",
      "final_count"
    )]
    
    # Calculate probes removed at each step
    probes_removed <- c(
      All_NA = counts$initial_count - counts$post_na_count,
      Non_CpG = counts$post_na_count - counts$post_nonCpG_count,
      SNP_Common = counts$post_nonCpG_count - counts$post_snp_common_count,
      SNP_GMAF1 = counts$post_snp_common_count - counts$post_snp_GMAF1_count,
      MASK_General = counts$post_snp_GMAF1_count - counts$post_mask_gen_count,
      GT20_Missing = counts$post_mask_gen_count - counts$post_gt20missing_probe_count,
      Cross_Reactive = counts$post_gt20missing_probe_count - counts$post_crossreactive_probe_count,
      ChrX_Y = counts$post_crossreactive_probe_count - counts$final_count,
      Final_Count = counts$final_count
    )
    
    # Extract cancer type from the file name (assuming format like TCGA-BRCA_methylation.rds)
    cancer_type <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(file))
    
    # Append the removal counts to the removal_table
    removal_table <- rbind(removal_table, data.frame(
      Cancer_Type = cancer_type,
      All_NA = probes_removed["All_NA"],
      Non_CpG = probes_removed["Non_CpG"],
      SNP_Common = probes_removed["SNP_Common"],
      SNP_GMAF1 = probes_removed["SNP_GMAF1"],
      MASK_General = probes_removed["MASK_General"],
      GT20_Missing = probes_removed["GT20_Missing"],
      Cross_Reactive = probes_removed["Cross_Reactive"],
      ChrX_Y = probes_removed["ChrX_Y"],
      Final_Count = probes_removed["Final_Count"],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    ))
    
  } else {
    # If there's a mismatch in sample names, throw an erroram
    stop(paste("Mismatch between column names and metadata samples in file:", file))
  }
}

reactable::reactable(removal_table,searchable = TRUE, resizable = TRUE)

```
